articles.title: Not All Browser APIs are "Web" APIs
articles.description: An interesting look at how some of the most popular APIs truly work, sharing how many of the web APIs we all use have third-party dependencies or are essentially standardized interfaces masking as vendor services. A good thing to be aware of for privacy, reliability and portability reasons.
articles.author: Kilian Valkhof

articles.title: 🌐  Introducing the <geolocation> Element
articles.description: As of Chrome 144, you can now use a new semantic <geolocation> HTML control for requesting user location data, moving away from a JavaScript-triggered prompt. There’s a Chrome-only demo here. There is cross-browser interest in this approach, but some concerns and issues remain — so keep in mind it’s not a global standard just yet, though there is a polyfill.
articles.author: Viana, Le, Steiner

articles.title: Firefox 147 Release Notes for Developers
articles.description: A sizeable release, with support for CSS anchor positioning, the Navigation API, CSS module scripts, view transition types, and WebGPU is now enabled on all Apple Silicon Macs.
articles.author: Mozilla

articles.title: Death to Scroll Fade!
articles.description: A neat effect perhaps? This article demonstrates why it may be more than a tad annoying in practice, along with the potential performance hit such an effect can bring.
articles.author: David Bushell

articles.title: Web Dependencies are Broken; Can We Fix Them?
articles.description: Lea delivers a compelling call to action on a problem many devs will have encountered: why is managing dependencies and introducing them into our code so unnecessarily messy and what should we do about it?
articles.author: Lea Verou

articles.title: What's the Minimum Markup Needed to Create a Modal?
articles.description: Your options for building a modal dialog without any (or as little as possible) JavaScript.
articles.author: Max Design

articles.title: Date is Out, Temporal is In
articles.description: The Temporal API has been promised as a future API tackling the weaknesses of JavaScript’s Date for years — that future is now finally arriving (not least in this week's Chrome 144 release).
articles.author: Mat “Wilto” Marquis

articles.title: Bytes I Can Delete After All This Time
articles.description: Thanks to advancements in CSS and JS there’s a growing number of techniques we no longer need — Remy shares a quick laundry list of just what we can ditch.
articles.author: Remy Sharp

articles.title: SVG Filters are Just Amazing
articles.description: Amit has been experimenting with what we can do with the filter property, and shares his findings here.
articles.author: Amit Merchant

articles.title: Fabric.js 7: A JavaScript HTML5 Canvas Library
articles.description: Provides an object model on top of canvas elements, as well as SVG-to-canvas and canvas-to-SVG features. There are also lots of demos, complete with code, to enjoy.
articles.author: Bogazzi, Nen, et al.

articles.title: HTML Minifier Next: A Powerful JavaScript-Based HTML Minifier
articles.description: A CLI-based HTML minifier tool that can also handle in-document CSS, JavaScript, and SVG minification. Jens shares an update on the project here.
articles.author: Jens Oliver Meiert

articles.title: jsPDF 4.0: Client-Side JavaScript PDF Generation
articles.description: Create tickets, documents, certificates, etc. all on the fly. There’s a live demo to try.
articles.author: Parallax

articles.title: Aether CSS: An Interactive App to Build UIs with Liquid Glass, Glassmorphism & Neumorphism
articles.description: You can choose from existing presets for each of the styles, or customize a preset’s values with various advanced settings. The full CSS & HTML is viewable to copy/paste.
articles.author: Dimitrije Djekanovic

articles.title: @vtbag: A Resource for Tools & Info on the View Transitions API
articles.description: If you want to get up to speed on View Transitions, this is a great place to start. Includes basic info, various tools and libraries, and a bunch of practical demos showing what’s possible.
articles.author: Martin Trapp

articles.title: 👃 FontSniff: AI-Powered Tool to Detect Fonts from Images
articles.description: Upload any image and the tool will attempt to identify fonts. Companion tools include tools for extracting text from images, including data tables in images.
articles.author: FontSniff
